summary.one_liner: A zero-dependency CLI (run with npx context-tax) that reads Claude Code session transcripts to show what gets sent to the model before your first prompt, what each item costs per use, and what to switch off.
summary.what_it_does: The tool reads local Claude Code session transcripts, which record the usage on each API reply and what was sent in the prompt (skill listing, tool names, instruction files, the client's own tools). It reports the per-turn token total from billed usage and itemises the rows: MCP servers, skills, agents, memory files, hooks and Claude Code's built-in tools and system prompt. It also counts the same transcripts for which tools and servers were actually called, so each item can be shown as a cost per use. A "fix" subcommand shows a diff of proposed settings changes, asks for confirmation, writes with backups, and prints commands for items declared in ~/.claude.json, which it does not edit. Other subcommands print a receipt without names, render a per-session turn-by-turn chart (terminal or SVG), and list resolved config and measurements. The README says it starts configured MCP servers to measure their tool lists, caches results for a week, and sends no telemetry.
use_cases: audit which MCP servers and tools are worth keeping
find skills that Claude Code sends without descriptions
measure fixed per-turn token overhead in Claude Code
trim unused built-in Claude Code tools via permissions.deny
share a context-cost receipt without exposing names or paths
review a long session's context growth and compactions
stack: MCP (Model Context Protocol) over stdio, streamable HTTP, and legacy SSE
notable: Measures cost per use by joining billed usage and transcript records with what was actually called, instead of estimating from config alone
Fix command shows the literal file diff before asking, backs up every replaced file, and never touches ~/.claude.json
Detects skills sent as bare names once the listing budget runs out and prices sending them all
Zero runtime dependencies, asserted by a test against the import graph
Receipt and session picture are designed to be shared with no server, skill, path or session names
caveats: Only works with Claude Code: config and transcript formats are specific to it; other clients would need a new reader
Measuring MCP servers requires starting them, and the README says a run can take about ten seconds per server timeout
Token counts are chars/4 estimates within about 4%, and no dollar figure is printed
Cannot tell which instructions inside CLAUDE.md or memory files were actually used
Items declared in ~/.claude.json or claude.ai connectors are handed back as commands or instructions rather than edited automatically
